claim: Peer-to-peer is absent on the CMP 170HX by default: torch.cuda.can_device_access_peer returns False for all 56 ordered pairs across 8 unlocked cards (0 of 56 capable), including pairs within a PIX group.
stance_target: The repo's premise that the box has no P2P, which underpins the DDP-only training-topology verdict
scope_conditions: 8 unlocked cards, all ordered pairs, PyTorch; ggml -lv 5 log shows zero peer/p2p/rpc occurrences; MIG 1g.64gb profile reports P2P No
quoted_support: torch.cuda.can_device_access_peer(i,j) | False for all 56 pairs (P2P-capable pairs: 0 of 56) | 8 unlocked cards, all pairs, including within a PIX group

claim: No branch of the unlock project contains any P2P enablement: a grep for 'p2p' and 'peer' across shipping master and all twelve unreleased branches returns only the stock nvidia-peermem.ko filename and one line of unmodified context.
stance_target: Whether any software path enables P2P on this card — none exists
scope_conditions: Grep of shipping master and 12 unreleased branches
quoted_support: A grep for p2p and peer across shipping master and all twelve unreleased branches returns exactly two kinds of hit: the stock nvidia-peermem.ko filename in the build.sh module install list, and one line of unmodified context (nv_uvm_resume_P2P(pUuid)) inside the Gen2 branch's 0008-pcie-gen2-probe-retrain.patch. No branch contains any P2P enablement.

claim: nvidia-peermem.ko is not GPU-to-GPU peer access — it is the stock peer-memory client that lets third-party RDMA hardware reach GPU memory, so seeing it built and loaded is not evidence of peer access.
stance_target: The common misreading that a loaded nvidia-peermem module implies P2P is available
scope_conditions: Module list includes nvidia.ko, nvidia-uvm.ko, nvidia-drm.ko and nvidia-peermem.ko
quoted_support: nvidia-peermem is the stock peer-memory client that lets third-party RDMA hardware reach GPU memory. Seeing it built and loaded ... is not evidence that GPU-to-GPU peer access is available.

claim: With layer-split inference on an 8-card, 80-layer model, every generated token makes 7 GPU-to-CPU-RAM-to-GPU hops with one NUMA crossing at the layer 49-to-50 transition, yielding only 2.25x aggregate scaling from 1 to 16 concurrent users.
stance_target: The measured cost of the missing P2P path on multi-GPU work
scope_conditions: 8-card rig, -sm layer split, 10 layers per GPU, one virtualised host whose link read Gen1 x4 with a device maximum of Gen2 x16
quoted_support: every generated token makes 7 GPU to CPU RAM to GPU hops, one of which crosses a NUMA/socket boundary at the layer 49 to 50 transition ... That is 2.25x aggregate scaling from 1 to 16 users

claim: Tensor parallelism is a measured dead end on these links: Qwen2.5-72B dense AWQ under vLLM at Gen1 x4 gives TP2 prefill of 316/420/416 t/s at 1k/4k/16k versus 839/1,092/960 for one card and 829/1,084/1,167 for PP2 — 2.3-2.8x worse prefill for only +23% decode.
stance_target: The repo's claim that TP is ruled out by the fabric, with a direct measurement rather than a judgement call
scope_conditions: Qwen2.5-72B dense AWQ, vLLM, Gen1 x4; decode 27.3 t/s (1 card), 29.1 (PP2), 33.7 (TP2)
quoted_support: TP2 (tensor) | 316 / 420 / 416 | 33.7 ... TP is 2.3-2.8x worse at prefill for +23% decode.

claim: The aikitoria P2P patch reportedly half-works on GA100: peer data movement runs at 6.25 GB/s versus 5.70 GB/s host-staged, but peer synchronisation fails and every NCCL collective hangs at transport connect with both GPUs pinned at 100%.
stance_target: Whether applying the P2P patch could improve DDP on this box — it would hang the all-reduce instead
scope_conditions: UNVERIFIED single-builder report on a four-card rig, logs posted but never independently reproduced; vLLM custom all-reduce hangs identically
quoted_support: peer data movement works and peer synchronisation does not ... Any NCCL collective | hangs at transport connect: no error, no timeout, both GPUs pinned at 100 %

claim: The reported mechanism for the half-working patch is that kbusIsPcieBar1P2PMappingSupported_GH100 requires static BAR1 spanning the whole framebuffer at a 512 MB-aligned offset, but the 170HX's BAR1 is 64 MB, so the check cannot pass and the mailbox fallback fails its alignment assertions.
stance_target: Why P2P cannot be made to work on this card even with a driver patch
scope_conditions: UNVERIFIED mechanism offered by the same single builder; kern_bus.c assertion (base & RM_PAGE_MASK) == 0 and kern_bus_gm200.c remoteWMBoxLocalAddr != ~0ULL
quoted_support: kbusIsPcieBar1P2PMappingSupported_GH100 requires static BAR1 on both GPUs, and static BAR1 requires BAR1 to span the whole framebuffer at a 512 MB-aligned offset. On the 170HX BAR1 is 64 MB, so the check cannot pass.

claim: The reporter's working multi-card vLLM configuration is NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 plus --disable-custom-all-reduce, which is exactly the configuration that works with no P2P patch at all — so the patch bought nothing for inference.
stance_target: Whether the P2P patch has any practical value for the box's workloads
scope_conditions: Same four-card rig as the half-working report
quoted_support: The reporter's working configuration for multi-card vLLM is NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 plus --disable-custom-all-reduce, which is exactly the configuration that works with no P2P patch at all. On that rig the patch therefore bought nothing for inference.

claim: p2pBandwidthLatencyTest has not been run on any 170HX, with or without the patch — nobody has posted a matrix — and the page calls this gap the single most important thing on it.
stance_target: How strong the evidence base for any P2P claim about this card actually is
scope_conditions: Measured-results table; P2P pairs capable unpatched 0 of 56 (high confidence); patch builds and loads yes (medium); effect on 170HX-only pairs reported none (low)
quoted_support: There are almost none, and the gap is the single most important thing on this page. ... p2pBandwidthLatencyTest on any 170HX | not run | nobody posted a matrix, with or without the patch

claim: The Blackwell reference P2P numbers (42.69-43.91 GB/s disabled, 55.59-56.58 GB/s enabled, 1,611-1,665 GB/s device-to-self) do not transfer to the 170HX, which at Gen1 or Gen2 x4 moves roughly one thirtieth to one sixtieth of those figures.
stance_target: Any use of modern P2P bandwidth figures to estimate what this box could do
scope_conditions: 9-GPU Blackwell system at Gen5 x16, not a 170HX; that driver branch lists only 3090/4090/5090 as supported
quoted_support: The Blackwell reference numbers do not transfer. A 170HX at Gen1 x4, or even Gen2 x4, moves roughly one thirtieth to one sixtieth of those figures

claim: Whether the P2P patch does anything on a 170HX-only host is an open problem: two same-day reports conflict superficially but may agree, since the successful rig also contained two RTX 3090s and the negative report says the patch only takes effect when other GPU models are present.
stance_target: Whether a 170HX-only multi-card host can ever get peer access
scope_conditions: One report of 'p2p + cmpunlock working' with a screenshot in a mixed rig; another that it 'doesn't seem to take effect on the 170HX'; no simpleP2P or p2pBandwidthLatencyTest output posted either way
quoted_support: One records getting "p2p + cmpunlock working" with a screenshot, in a rig that also contained two RTX 3090s. Another records that after a successful build "it doesn't seem to take effect on the 170HX ... it only has an effect on them if there are other models of GPUs on the same machine".

claim: BAR1 peer DMA requires the IOMMU in passthrough mode (iommu=pt), which the fork's own README calls 'very dangerous if you run untrusted software or devices', and ACS on the root ports forces GPU-to-GPU traffic up through the CPU root complex unless disabled — which in turn breaks IOMMU group isolation.
stance_target: The security and configuration cost of attempting P2P on this box
scope_conditions: P2P branch setup: amd_iommu=on iommu=pt or intel_iommu=on iommu=pt; ACS remedies are BIOS disable, pcie_acs_override=downstream,multifunction, or an ACS override kernel patch
quoted_support: The README states the requirement flatly: IOMMU must be in passthrough mode, not translating, or DMA goes through IOMMU page tables and transfers fail. ... this configuration "is very dangerous if you run untrusted software or devices".

claim: The Gen2 code already configures exactly what the P2P patch requires (commit 6a85e6c appends intel_iommu=on iommu=pt or amd_iommu=on iommu=pt and verifies passthrough at runtime), making Gen2-plus-P2P the closest thing to a pre-configured stack anyone could assemble today — and nobody has assembled it.
stance_target: Whether a Gen2+P2P configuration has ever been tested end to end
scope_conditions: Gen2 installer branch code, not shipping; runtime check greps iommu=pt from /proc/cmdline and inspects /sys/class/iommu
quoted_support: the Gen2 code already configures exactly what the P2P patch requires, which makes Gen2-plus-P2P the closest thing to a pre-configured stack anyone could assemble today. Nobody has assembled it.
